```python
import sys

def solve():
    line = sys.stdin.readline().strip()
    if not line:
        return
    # parse row number and seat letter
    n_str = line[:-1]
    seat = line[-1]
    n = int(n_str)
    
    # Determine block (pair of rows served together) and block index
    # Blocks: (1,3), (2,4), (5,7), (6,8), (9,11), (10,12), ...
    # Block index i: 0-based
    if n % 2 == 1:
        block_num = (n - 1) // 4  # 0,1,2,... for odd rows 1,5,9,... (first attendant) and 3,7,11,... (second attendant)
        i = 2 * block_num
        # Check if n is first attendant row (4*block_num + 1) or second (4*block_num + 3)
        if n % 4 == 1:
            # first attendant
            pass
        else:
            # second attendant
            i += 1
    else:
        block_num = (n - 2) // 4
        i = 2 * block_num
        if n % 4 == 2:
            # first attendant
            pass
        else:
            # second attendant
            i += 1
    
    # Time before block i
    # i blocks completed: each block serves 2 rows * 6 seats = 12 seconds serving time
    # movement time: sequence of moves: after block 0 move 1, after block 1 move 3, after block 2 move 1, after block 3 move 3, ...
    # number of complete moves before block i = i moves (since before block 0 there are 0 moves)
    # For i moves, number of 1-moves = (i + 1) // 2, number of 3-moves = i // 2
    num_one_moves = (i + 1) // 2
    num_three_moves = i // 2
    movement_time = num_one_moves * 1 + num_three_moves * 3
    serving_time_prev_blocks = i * 12
    time_before_block = serving_time_prev_blocks + movement_time
    
    # Time within the block
    # Determine if Vasya is served by first or second attendant
    # The pair of rows in block i: 
    # We can compute first attendant row and second attendant row for block i
    # From pattern:
    # i=0: rows 1 (first), 3 (second)
    # i=1: rows 2 (first), 4 (second)
    # i=2: rows 5 (first), 7 (second)
    # i=3: rows 6 (first), 8 (second)
    # i=4: rows 9 (first), 11 (second)
    # i=5: rows 10 (first), 12 (second)
    # General: for even i=2k: first row = 4k+1, second row = 4k+3
    #          for odd i=2k+1: first row = 4k+2, second row = 4k+4
    if i % 2 == 0:
        k = i // 2
        first_row = 4 * k + 1
        second_row = 4 * k + 3
    else:
        k = (i - 1) // 2
        first_row = 4 * k + 2
        second_row = 4 * k + 4
    
    # Time for serving within block: second attendant finishes 6 seconds after first attendant starts? Actually both serve simultaneously but offset by row?
    # Both attendants serve their own rows simultaneously. They start at same time (after moving).
    # They each take 6 seconds to serve their row.
    # The serving order in a row: right side (d,e,f) then left side (a,b,c), from window to aisle.
    # Right side seats: f, e, d (window to aisle)
    # Left side seats: a, b, c (window to aisle)
    # So order: f (1), e (2), d (3), a (4), b (5), c (6)
    seat_order = {'f':1, 'e':2, 'd':3, 'a':4, 'b':5, 'c':6}
    offset = seat_order[seat]
    
    if n == first_row:
        # served by first attendant, starts at time_before_block
        total_time = time_before_block + offset
    else:
        # served by second attendant, also starts at time_before_block (simultaneously)
        total_time = time_before_block + offset
    
    print(total_time)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    solve()
```

source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Print one integer — the number of seconds Vasya has to wait until he gets his lunch.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The only line of input contains a description of Vasya's seat in the format ns, where n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1018) is the index of the row and s is the seat in this row, denoted as letter from 'a' to 'f'. The index of the row and the seat are not separated by a space.
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteIn the first sample, the first flight attendant serves Vasya first, so Vasya gets his lunch after 1 second.In the second sample, the flight attendants will spend 6 seconds to serve everyone in the rows 1 and 3, then they will move one row forward in 1 second. As they first serve seats located to the right of the aisle in order from window to aisle, Vasya has to wait 3 more seconds. The total is 6 + 1 + 3 = 10.
source_data.prob_desc_description: A new airplane SuperPuperJet has an infinite number of rows, numbered with positive integers starting with 1 from cockpit to tail. There are six seats in each row, denoted with letters from 'a' to 'f'. Seats 'a', 'b' and 'c' are located to the left of an aisle (if one looks in the direction of the cockpit), while seats 'd', 'e' and 'f' are located to the right. Seats 'a' and 'f' are located near the windows, while seats 'c' and 'd' are located near the aisle.    It's lunch time and two flight attendants have just started to serve food. They move from the first rows to the tail, always maintaining a distance of two rows from each other because of the food trolley. Thus, at the beginning the first attendant serves row 1 while the second attendant serves row 3. When both rows are done they move one row forward: the first attendant serves row 2 while the second attendant serves row 4. Then they move three rows forward and the first attendant serves row 5 while the second attendant serves row 7. Then they move one row forward again and so on.Flight attendants work with the same speed: it takes exactly 1 second to serve one passenger and 1 second to move one row forward. Each attendant first serves the passengers on the seats to the right of the aisle and then serves passengers on the seats to the left of the aisle (if one looks in the direction of the cockpit). Moreover, they always serve passengers in order from the window to the aisle. Thus, the first passenger to receive food in each row is located in seat 'f', and the last one — in seat 'c'. Assume that all seats are occupied.Vasya has seat s in row n and wants to know how many seconds will pass before he gets his lunch.
